seed: Separating a capture and then reading every run of text in it, on the settings pane fixture. The study this began as is finished (docs/design/separate-reads-the-words.md, answered no automatic reading), and the app has moved on since: a separated run already says its own words on its row, because the separation reads them for the NAME. So what this walk holds today is the part that is still true either way. Separating hands back nine runs, named after the words in them and every one still a PICTURE; asking for the words run by run makes each one real text, which the dock shows by growing a Text section; and each reading is its own undo step, so one press takes back one label.

steps.note: the capture as it opens: one locked Background picture and nothing else

What the command does today: nine runs of text are their own layers, each row saying the words in it because the separation read them for its name (SeparatedBoxNames). A name is all that was read. Every one of them is still a PICTURE of a label, so changing any of these words is a second command away and a person has to know it exists.
ONE undo press takes the whole separation back: nineteen layers and the repaired bitmap go together, and the screenshot is one locked Background again. That is the promise any new shape has to keep.

Every one of the nine runs is real text now, wearing its own words: nine of nine cleared the bar on this capture. The canvas is meant to look untouched, and so is the layers list, which is the finding the study ended on: the rows said these words before any of them was read, so the list cannot tell you which are words and which are still pictures. The dock can. The run picked here has a Text section under it, with a face, a size and the alignment buttons, where a picture has none.

Asked for run by run, each reading is its own undo step, so one press takes back ONE label: the Save Changes run is a picture again, with no Text section under it, and the other eight are still words. Its row says the same thing either way, which is exactly why the dock is where this has to be read.
